newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet fuel supported despite glut.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet fuel supported despite glut.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel prices on Tuesday continued to receive support from a Singapore trader's purchases despite a well-supplied regional market and soft demand, traders said.
They said a U.S. trader is bringing in jet fuel cargoes into the region.

Two 100,000-barrel cargoes were sold by a European major on Tuesday at higher levels for May 18-22 lifting on a free-on-board (fob) basis. One cargo was purchased by a Singapore trader at $25.30 per barrel, and the second by a Japanese trader at $25.00.
Another cargo was being discussed at $24.70 for May 7-11 lifting. Tuesday's purchases brought the volumes traded since last week to 800,000 barrels.

Gas oil continued to be actively traded with a total of 600,000 barrels exchanging hands on Tuesday. The purchases brought total purchases by two Singapore traders so far to around 15 million barrels since March 3.

The sister company of a Singapore trader bought four cargoes between $26.60 and $27.50 per barrel with early May cargoes traded higher than second half May cargoes. Sellers were a Japanese trader, a US major and another European major.
Traders said despite these trades, open requirements from countries in the region appeared sketchy.
